title: Tenant‑anchored export templates and pricing‑slicer triage
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Background: Enterprise customers routinely request tenant-scoped exports for cost allocation, per-team usage slices, and ad-hoc CSV/Parquet dumps for downstream finance/BI ingestion. Current intake we have is ad-hoc: product-support tickets, Drive requests, and occasional Slack pings. That creates duplicated work across SRE/PM/Eng and mismatched expectations on delivery format and SLAs.

Goal: Establish a deterministic triage flow and a set of reusable 'tenant-anchored' export templates (structured CSV/Parquet schemas + per-tenant cost breakdown mapping) and a pricing-slicer taxonomy that lets us quickly classify requests, estimate effort, and route to the right delivery lane (self-serve, config assist, eng-delivered). This ticket covers intake form updates, priority rules, example templates, and routing matrix for enterprise console/reporting requests.

Scope (what this ticket will do):
- Design and publish 3 export template schemas: cost-breakdown-by-route, usage-timeseries-by-token-type, and workspace-level-aggregates-for-billing.
- Define pricing-slicer taxonomy (e.g., committed vs usage-bucket, embedding-heavy vs generation-heavy) used to estimate compute cost and SLA.
- Create a triage decision tree and routing matrix for requests (self-serve template, low-effort PM-config, eng custom export).
- Update intake form in Console and Support playbook + add required fields for security/KYC/pass-through encryption needs.
- Produce a short runbook for Solutions Engineers with sample queries, BigQuery/Parquet examples, and cost-estimation heuristic.

Out of scope: Building the export pipeline, long-term analytics UI, or billing system changes — those will be follow-up tickets after template and triage design are agreed.
acceptance_criteria: A public Confluence doc exists with the 3 export template schemas and example payloads (CSV/Parquet) and mapping to Console UI fields.
An intake form (Console + Support) includes the new required fields (tenant_id, reporting_period, desired_format, anonymization_needed, encryption_at_rest) and routes requests based on taxonomy.
Routing matrix documented: >=90% of past 30 enterprise export requests would be correctly routed to self-serve or PM-config lanes when applied retrospectively.
Solutions Engineering runbook with sample BigQuery SQL and cost-slicer examples published and reviewed by SE leads.
Triage SLA and priority scoring (P0/P1/P2) calibrated and signed off by PM and Support manager.
notes: Prioritization rationale: enterprise exports are high visibility for finance teams and often lead to upsell or churn avoidance — high customer impact but often small engineering effort if we standardize templates.
Trade-offs discussed with Eng: favoring well-documented templates reduces on-call/hand-holding but requires initial PM/SE investment to create canonical queries and sample data.
